TLDR;

8 pseudopatients (including 3 psychologists, a pediatrician, & a psychiatrist) were admitted to various mental hospitals by initially faking a mental disorder. After admittance, each had to get out on their own by proving their sanity by simply being normal/sane.

All of the pseudopatients were discharged (after an average of 19 days). But the study emphasizes they were only dismissed in a state of remission,

If the pseudopatient was to be discharged, he must naturally be "in remission"; but he was not sane, nor, in the institution's view, had he ever been sane.

They concluded:

...the evidence is strong that, once labeled schizophrenic, the pseudopatient was stuck with that label. [...] Failure to detect sanity during the course of hospitalization may be due to the fact that physicians operate with a strong bias...that physicians are more inclined to call a healthy person sick than a sick person healthy.

Interestingly, staffers never suspected the pseudopatients deception, that they were in fact sane. However, "It was quite common for the patients to "detect" the pseudopatient's sanity."

A later study informed hospitals that pseudopatients would be admitted & they were to detect these impostors. Of 193 patients, 41 were deemed to be pseudopatients with high confidence by at least one staffer. But in fact, no pseudopatients were ever admitted.
Playing a bit of devil's advocate, for the sake of debate: isn't it better to lean towards false diagnosis than not diagnosing an actual disorder?

Sure, with extreme disorders that can lead to self-harm or violent outbursts. However, if there is no reason to suspect those things it can really fuck up a person's life being diagnosed with some bullshit disorder. For example, being diagnosed with ADD as a child disqualifies people for a lot of jobs.
